title: Living with COPD
what: COPD is a lung disease that makes breathing harder. Treatment and lifestyle help slow it and ease breathlessness.
why: If a doctor found COPD, most often in people who smoked or breathed dust and smoke for a long time.
duration: treatment is usually ongoing, with check-ups on a schedule
tell_doctor: Whether you smoke now, since your doctor can help you quit
How often you have flare-ups and shortness of breath
Which inhalers you use and how
If swelling appeared on your legs

prepare.title: Quitting smoking
prepare.text: This is the most important thing. Ask your doctor for help, which makes quitting easier.

prepare.title: Inhalers
prepare.text: Show your doctor how you use them.

prepare.title: Vaccines
prepare.text: Ask your doctor about flu and pneumococcal vaccines.

bring: A diary of how you feel
steps: Use your inhalers every day as your doctor prescribed
Move every day: walk at a calm pace
Do the breathing exercises your doctor taught you
When short of breath, breathe through pursed lips: in through the nose, a long breath out through the mouth
Avoid smoke, dust, and cold air
feel: Shortness of breath when active is common, and training reduces it
A morning cough with phlegm is common
after: Notice the signs of a flare-up: more breathlessness, more phlegm, or phlegm that changed color
In a flare-up, contact your doctor right away
Ask about a pulmonary rehab program
red_flags: Severe shortness of breath at rest, or it is hard to talk: call emergency services
Blue lips, confusion, or drowsiness: call emergency services

faq.q: Is there any point in quitting smoking if I already have the disease?
faq.a: Yes. It slows the disease at any age.

faq.q: Do I need oxygen at home?
faq.a: Only some people do. Your doctor decides based on tests.

reminders.text: Morning inhaler and a short walk at a calm pace.
